headline: CROP TOUR WEEK OPENS QUIET; WHEAT FIRMS
subheadline: Corn and beans drift near unchanged as Pro Farmer crop tour gets underway; wheat adds 4 cents on its own momentum.
lead: Most markets barely moved today. Corn added a penny and a half to $4.38, beans gave back 3 cents to $11.69, and the whole complex is marking time ahead of Pro Farmer crop tour results later this week. Wheat at $6.40 is the one market with a pulse. Today is position-holding, not position-making. Wait.
the_takeaway: Crop tour week starts quiet; wheat is the only market with a reason to move.
teaser: Pro Farmer tour launches, grains tread water, wheat firms 4 cents on its own.

one_number.context: Hogs at $84.85 sit at just the 23rd percentile of their 52-week range, even after Friday's big run. Finland's first-ever African Swine Fever detection near the Russian border is the tail risk that could reprice that floor fast.

yesterdays_call.summary: Called wheat up toward $6.55; wheat closed today at $6.40, firming 4 cents but well short of the $6.55 line.
yesterdays_call.note: The directional lean was right but $6.55 never came into play; call it a partial at best, graded as a miss on the level.

sections.title: Grains Tread Water
sections.body:
- Corn at **$4.38** added a penny and a half, the kind of session where nobody adds conviction ahead of crop tour; the 2026 planting season, behind through May before catching up between rain systems, left plenty of Belt uncertainty that Pro Farmer scouts will start resolving this week.
- Beans at $11.69 gave back 3 cents on fund and technical selling, still working off last week's weather-and-war premium removal that Agweb flagged Friday as a potential overshoot.
- Neither market is breaking new ground; the dough-and-dent corn crop is trading on what tour scouts see, not what traders think they know.
sections.catalyst: Pro Farmer crop tour underway; last week's steep grain losses on favorable Belt weather removal of risk premium.
sections.bottom_line: Crop tour data, not today's price action, writes the next chapter.

sections.title: Wheat Firms Quietly
sections.body:
- Chicago wheat settled at **$6.40**, up just over 4 cents, the only grain with any real directional energy today.
- The Agweb Friday piece questioned whether last week's war-and-weather premium removal went too far; wheat's bounce today is thin, but it is the market making that same argument with its own money.
- Watch the watch list level to know if this is real; today's close does not answer that question.
sections.bottom_line: Wheat firms, but one day of 4-cent buying does not overrule the sell-off -- check the watch list trigger before adding exposure.

sections.title: Livestock Quiet; Milk Breaks
sections.body:
- Live cattle at **$231.75** and feeders at $343.77 both edged up fractions; the cash trade that was 'elusive' Friday per Brownfield is still the missing piece, and nobody's pushing futures without it.
- Lean hogs added 1.9% to $84.85, continuing Friday's momentum, with Finland's first-ever ASF detection near its Russian border adding a quiet structural floor argument.
- Class III Milk fell 2.7% to $17.16, the sharpest move in the complex today; dairy producers without August-September hedge coverage are watching a 52-week range position that keeps sliding toward the bottom half.
sections.catalyst: Cattle cash trade absent Friday per Brownfield; Finland ASF detection adds hog floor argument; Class III continues lower.
sections.bottom_line: Cattle waiting on cash, hogs building a floor, milk is the morning's real loser.
sections.farmer_action: Dairy: Class III at $17.16 with no hedge is exposed. Look at August and September floor options before Tuesday's open.

sections.title: Energy Eases; Inputs Quiet
sections.body:
- WTI crude at **$78.83** slipped 1.2%, with Kuwait's July production running at 1.97 million barrels per day as OPEC+ completes its output cut reversal, adding global supply pressure.
- Iran-Hormuz tensions, with the Strait of Hormuz premium that built since early April now deflating on diplomatic progress, got a footnote today: a Greek LNG carrier cleared the Strait after an incident at week's end, vessel stable, lanes navigable.
- Natural gas at $2.77 barely moved; at the 5th percentile of its 52-week range, it has more upside math than story right now.
sections.catalyst: Kuwait July crude output ran sharply higher as OPEC+ reverses cuts; Hormuz LNG incident resolved without escalation.
sections.bottom_line: Crude supply building, Hormuz premium still deflating; no input cost surprise today.

outside_the_pit.title: John Deere Right-to-Repair Settlement Reaches Resolution
outside_the_pit.body: The long-running antitrust lawsuit against Deere has closed, giving independent operators more repair access. For producers, this means real leverage on dealership service pricing and repair timelines during critical planting and harvest windows.

outside_the_pit.title: High Plains Drought Raising Anthrax Risk for Livestock Producers
outside_the_pit.body: Prolonged hot, dry conditions across the High Plains are elevating anthrax risk even without active cases reported. Producers grazing cattle in affected areas should review vaccination status now; an outbreak during weaning season compounds financial damage fast.

weekly_thread.question: Will Pro Farmer crop tour data add a weather premium back into corn and beans, or confirm the Belt is on pace?
weekly_thread.status_text: Tour launches today with corn in dough and dent; grains are treading water until scouts report yield estimates mid-week.

the_more_you_know.title: The Carry Spread Is the Crop Tour's Lie Detector
the_more_you_know.body: Corn's nearby at $4.38 versus December at $4.62 is a 24-cent carry. That spread widens when the market doubts the current crop and narrows when supply looks comfortable. Watch whether Pro Farmer yield estimates this week move that spread more than the outright price; the carry tells you what the funds actually believe about the harvest.

watch_list.desc: USDA Crop Progress: corn condition rating above 65% good/excellent keeps the weather premium out; below 60% puts it back on the table.
Pro Farmer crop tour yield estimates: corn below 177 bu/acre adds weather premium; above 181 keeps the recent sell-off intact.
Weekly export sales: beans under 400K MT confirms the chart, not demand, is driving price right now.
Wheat: $6.55 is the line that has to break to confirm last week's sell-off was overdone.

daily_quote.text: It is in the shelter of each other that the people live.
